description: Comprehensive reference catalog of ecclesial communities for tracing breakaway lineages from the Catholic Church, including groups at separation_degree > 1 (broke from a prior breakaway rather than directly from Rome). Primary use: next-phase graph of Christian separations.

root.name: Catholic Church
root.notes: Root node for lineage distance. Not a breakaway.

schema.name: display name
schema.separation_degree: shortest primary lineage distance from catholic-church
schema.lineage: ordered ids from catholic-church to this group
schema.notes: Lineages for restorationist/charismatic/AIC bodies are sometimes heuristic.

preference: Prefer durable communal identities. Mark contested cases. Synthetic umbrella nodes exist only to support lineage edges. Degree counts follow the primary broke_from chain, not every historical influence.

groups.name: Eastern Catholic churches (Uniates)
groups.summary: NOT breakaways: Byzantine, Maronite, Chaldean, Syro-Malabar, etc., in communion with Rome.
groups.notes: Sentinel against mis-tagging Eastern Catholics as Orthodox breakaways.

groups.name: Maronites
groups.summary: NOT a breakaway: Eastern Catholic church in communion with Rome. Included to prevent misclassification.
groups.notes: Degree 0 sentinel.

groups.name: Novatianists
groups.summary: Rigorist schism over lapsi; lasting parallel hierarchy for centuries.

groups.name: Melitian schism (Egypt)
groups.summary: Egyptian rigorist schism contemporary with early Arian controversies.

groups.name: Donatists
groups.summary: North African rigorist church rejecting traditor clergy and Catholic episcopal legitimacy.

groups.name: Arian churches
groups.summary: Communities and royal churches refusing Nicene homoousios; Homoean/Arian ecclesial structures among Goths, Vandals, Lombards.

groups.name: Assyrian Church of the East
groups.approx_rupture: 431 (same as Church of the East modern name)
groups.summary: Modern name of the historic Church of the East patriarchate (often overlapping id with church-of-the-east).
groups.notes: Near-duplicate of church-of-the-east for common naming; prefer church-of-the-east as canonical id when linking.

groups.name: Church of the East
groups.region: Persian Empire / East Syria / Central Asia / China (historical)
groups.summary: East Syriac dyophysite communion not accepting Ephesus’s condemnation of Nestorius.

groups.name: Armenian Apostolic Church
groups.summary: National church rejecting Chalcedon; later Florence union attempt with Armenians.

groups.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
groups.summary: Alexandrian miaphysite patriarchate after Chalcedon; head of much African Oriental Orthodoxy.

groups.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
groups.summary: Tewahedo church in the Oriental Orthodox family; historically under Coptic guidance then autocephalous.

groups.name: Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church
groups.summary: Indian Oriental Orthodox church of West Syriac liturgy; complex later splits with Jacobite and Catholic factions.

groups.name: Oriental Orthodox churches
groups.region: Egypt, Syria, Armenia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, India
groups.summary: Non-Chalcedonian (miaphysite) family: Coptic, Syriac, Armenian, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Malankara.

groups.name: Syriac Orthodox Church
groups.summary: West Syriac miaphysite patriarchate of Antioch (Jacobite).

groups.name: Eastern Orthodox churches
groups.summary: Byzantine-rite autocephalous churches out of full communion with Rome after the East–West schism.

groups.name: Cathars / Albigensians
groups.summary: Dualist/dissenting networks opposed by crusade and Inquisition; no surviving organized communion.
groups.notes: Contested durability as a ‘church’.

groups.name: Waldensians
groups.summary: Poor of Lyons dissenting movement forming lasting communities; later joined Reformed Protestantism.

groups.name: Wycliffites / Lollards
groups.summary: English Wycliffite/Lollard reform networks condemned at Constance.

groups.name: Hussites
groups.summary: Bohemian reform communion after Hus; Utraquist and Taborite wings.

groups.name: Lutheran churches
groups.summary: Evangelical churches of the Augsburg Confession rejecting papal jurisdiction and Tridentine soteriology/sacraments.

groups.name: Reformed / Calvinist churches
groups.summary: Magisterial Reformed communions (Zwinglian/Calvinist) rejecting Roman jurisdiction and Catholic sacramental order.

groups.name: Anabaptist / Radical Reformation churches
groups.region: Central Europe; later North America / global
groups.summary: Radical Reformation bodies practicing believers’ baptism and often separation from magisterial churches.

groups.name: Anglican Communion / Church of England
groups.summary: English national church rejecting papal jurisdiction; later Anglican Communion provinces.

groups.name: Old Catholic churches (Union of Utrecht)
groups.summary: Communions rejecting Vatican I papal infallibility/primacy definitions.

groups.name: Polish National Catholic Church
groups.summary: Independent Catholic jurisdiction among Polish immigrants; historically allied with Old Catholics.

groups.name: Philippine Independent Church (Aglipayan)
groups.summary: National church separating from Rome under Gregorio Aglipay amid colonial transition.

groups.name: Brazilian Catholic Apostolic Church
groups.summary: Independent Catholic church founded by Carlos Duarte Costa.

groups.name: Chinese Catholic Patriotic Association structures
groups.summary: State-supervised Catholic structures with contested communion claims regarding Rome.
groups.notes: Politically entangled; contested as classic breakaway.

groups.name: Sedevacantist independent chapels and societies
groups.summary: Bodies holding the post-conciliar Holy See vacant; separate sacramental networks (e.g. CMRI, SSPV).

groups.name: Society of St. Pius X
groups.summary: Traditionalist society rejecting aspects of Vatican II reception while claiming Catholic identity.
groups.notes: Claims same communion; irregular in Roman eyes.

groups.name: Palmarian Catholic Church
groups.summary: Conclavist church with its own papacy centered at El Palmar de Troya.

groups.name: Unitas Fratrum / Moravian Church
groups.summary: Bohemian Brethren emerging from Hussite reform; renewed at Herrnhut as Moravian Church.

groups.name: Hutterites
groups.summary: Communal Anabaptist tradition under Jakob Hutter.

groups.name: Mennonite churches
groups.summary: Anabaptist tradition associated with Menno Simons; multiple conferences worldwide.

groups.name: Presbyterian churches
groups.summary: Reformed churches with Presbyterian polity; often treated as the Scottish/English expression of Reformed rather than a later break.
groups.notes: Degree 2 as national/polity differentiation within Reformed; still useful for lineage tracing.

groups.name: Unitarian / Unitarian Universalist churches
groups.summary: Anti-Trinitarian and later liberal Protestant bodies; Anglo-American Unitarianism largely from Congregational/Reformed roots.
groups.notes: Multiple origins; Transylvanian Unitarianism is early; US UU merges Unitarian and Universalist.

groups.name: English Separatists / Congregationalists
groups.summary: Separatist and non-separating Puritan congregational churches leaving Anglican settlement.

groups.name: Congregationalist / New England Protestant milieu
groups.summary: Synthetic/near-duplicate of Puritan Separatist congregational culture for attaching New England-born movements.

groups.name: Russian Old Believers
groups.summary: Split from Russian Orthodoxy over Nikonian liturgical reforms; popovtsy and bespopovtsy wings.

groups.name: Pietist and Haugean movements
groups.summary: Renewal movements within Lutheranism; some remained inside, some formed free churches.

groups.name: Methodist churches
groups.summary: Wesleyan movement that formed separate churches from Anglican structures.

groups.name: Swedenborgian / New Church
groups.summary: Churches based on Emanuel Swedenborg’s revelations; emerged in Lutheran/Anglican cultural settings.

groups.name: Protestant mission churches (umbrella)
groups.summary: Synthetic node for mission-founded Protestant churches used when an AIC’s precise parent mission is mixed.
groups.notes: Graph convenience node, not a single historical communion.

groups.name: Plymouth Brethren
groups.summary: Restorationist evangelical assemblies rejecting denominationalism; Open and Exclusive wings.

groups.name: Dutch Reformed secession churches (Afscheiding/Doleantie)
groups.summary: 19th-c. orthodox secessions from state Dutch Reformed Church; roots of CRCNA/Gereformeerde kerken.

groups.name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church
groups.summary: Reformed Oriental/West Syriac church influenced by Anglican CMS; distinct from both Rome and Malankara Orthodoxy.

groups.name: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod
groups.summary: Confessional US Lutheran synod; differentiation within Lutheranism rather than a new religion.

groups.name: African Instituted Churches (AIC umbrella)
groups.summary: Umbrella for African-founded churches separating from mission Protestantism/Catholicism (e.g. Zionist, Aladura, Kimbanguist).
groups.notes: Parent is heterogeneous (often Anglican/Methodist/Baptist missions); degree path is approximate.

groups.name: Jacobite Syrian Christian Church (Malankara)
groups.summary: Malankara faction under Syriac Orthodox patriarch vs autocephalous Malankara Orthodox.

groups.name: Iglesia ni Cristo
groups.summary: Restorationist Philippine church founded by Felix Manalo; distinct from Aglipayan Catholicism.
groups.notes: Historical relation to Aglipayan milieu is debated; alternative: treat as degree-1 restorationist from Catholic culture.

groups.name: Liberal Catholic Church
groups.summary: Theosophically influenced independent sacramental church deriving orders via Old Catholic lines.
groups.notes: Degree 2 via Old Catholic succession; not a direct Roman doctrinal council break.

groups.name: Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia (ROCOR)
groups.summary: Emigré Russian Orthodox jurisdiction; reconciled with Moscow Patriarchate in 2007 though some splinters remain separate.
groups.notes: Contested as lasting breakaway after 2007 reconciliation.

groups.name: Greek Old Calendarists
groups.summary: Greek jurisdictions rejecting the Revised Julian calendar; subset of True Orthodox phenomenon.

groups.name: True Orthodox / Old Calendarist churches
groups.summary: Jurisdictions rejecting mainstream Orthodox calendar reforms and/or perceived ecumenism.

groups.name: Evangelical Free Church
groups.summary: Free-church evangelical tradition with Scandinavian Lutheran free-church ancestry.

groups.name: Ancient Church of the East
groups.summary: Calendar/jurisdiction split from the Assyrian Church of the East.
groups.notes: Broke from Church of the East (degree 1 from Catholic), not from Oriental Orthodox.

groups.name: Continuing Anglican churches
groups.summary: Jurisdictions leaving Canterbury/ECUSA Communion over prayer book, ordination, and doctrinal changes (Congress of St. Louis).

groups.name: Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church
groups.summary: Autocephalous Oriental Orthodox church separated from Ethiopian Orthodox after Eritrean independence.
groups.notes: Degree 2 relative to Catholic via Ethiopian/Oriental Orthodox lineage.

groups.name: Ethiopian–Eritrean Tewahedo separation
groups.summary: Alias/summary node pointing to eritrean-orthodox autocephaly.
groups.notes: Prefer eritrean-orthodox for links.

groups.name: Anglican Church in North America
groups.summary: Realignment province formed by conservatives leaving The Episcopal Church / ACC.

groups.name: Baptist churches
groups.summary: Believers’-baptism churches emerging from English Separatism (General/Particular Baptists); later global family.
groups.notes: Some historians also stress continental Anabaptist influence; primary English lineage via Separatism.

groups.name: Religious Society of Friends (Quakers)
groups.summary: Fox’s Friends movement arising in the English Civil War religious ferment.

groups.name: Amish
groups.summary: Jakob Ammann split from Swiss Mennonites over discipline and shunning.

groups.name: Restoration Movement (Stone–Campbell)
groups.summary: American restorationists seeking New Testament church pattern; Churches of Christ / Christian Churches / Disciples.

groups.name: African Methodist Episcopal Church
groups.summary: Black Methodist denomination founded by Richard Allen amid racial exclusion.

groups.name: African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church
groups.summary: Independent Black Methodist body formed in New York.

groups.name: Wesleyan Church
groups.summary: Wesleyan-Holiness denomination with roots in abolitionist Methodist splits.

groups.name: Exclusive Brethren (Darbyite)
groups.summary: Darbyite Exclusive assemblies separating from Open Brethren.

groups.name: Free Methodist Church
groups.summary: Holiness Methodist split emphasizing free pews and sanctification.

groups.name: Salvation Army
groups.summary: Booth’s Wesleyan mission that became a distinct quasi-military church organization.

groups.name: Holiness movement churches
groups.summary: Wesleyan-holiness denominations emphasizing entire sanctification (e.g. Church of the Nazarene roots, Pilgrim Holiness).

groups.name: Christian Methodist Episcopal Church
groups.summary: Black Methodist church organized from the Methodist Episcopal Church, South.

groups.name: Church of Christ, Scientist
groups.summary: Eddy’ s Christian Science church arising in New England Protestant culture.
groups.notes: broke_from uses congregational/New England Protestant milieu; not a clean jurisdictional split.

groups.name: Christian and Missionary Alliance
groups.summary: Simpson’s deeper-life missionary movement becoming a denomination.

groups.name: Kimbanguist Church
groups.summary: Church of Jesus Christ on Earth founded by Simon Kimbangu.

groups.name: Aladura churches
groups.summary: Prayer-healing AIC family (e.g. Christ Apostolic Church, Cherubim and Seraphim).

groups.name: United Church of Christ
groups.summary: US merger of Congregational Christian and Evangelical & Reformed churches.

groups.name: Seventh Day Baptist churches
groups.summary: Sabbatarian Baptists; earlier than Seventh-day Adventists.

groups.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
groups.summary: Smith’s restorationist church; claims pristine restoration rather than reform of Protestantism. Placed near American restoration milieu for tracing.
groups.notes: Self-understanding is not ‘Protestant breakaway’; degree path is heuristic for graph distance from Catholic Church.

groups.name: Millerite / Adventist movement
groups.summary: Second Great Awakening advent expectation; parent of Seventh-day Adventists and other advent bodies. Mixed Baptist/Christian Connexion roots.

groups.name: Southern Baptist Convention
groups.summary: US Baptist split over slavery/missions organization; largest US Protestant denomination historically.

groups.name: Church of God (Anderson)
groups.summary: Holiness restorationist movement under D. S. Warner.

groups.name: Churches of Christ (a cappella)
groups.summary: Conservative Restoration branch opposing instruments and missionary societies.

groups.name: Pentecostal churches
groups.summary: Classical Pentecostal denominations emerging from Holiness revival (Azusa Street, etc.).

groups.name: Church of the Nazarene
groups.summary: Major Holiness denomination consolidated from Methodist-holiness bodies.

groups.name: Messianic Jewish congregations
groups.summary: Congregations affirming Jesus as Messiah while retaining Jewish identity; diverse Protestant evangelical parentage.
groups.notes: Parentage mixed; Baptist/evangelical link is heuristic.

groups.name: Community of Christ (RLDS)
groups.summary: Reorganized Latter Day Saint church under Joseph Smith III lineage.

groups.name: Seventh-day Adventist Church
groups.summary: Sabbatarian Adventist denomination organized after the Great Disappointment.

groups.name: Bible Student movement
groups.summary: Russell’s Bible Student movement emerging from adventist/restorationist milieu.

groups.name: Assemblies of God
groups.summary: Largest classical Pentecostal fellowship, organized at Hot Springs, Arkansas.

groups.name: Oneness Pentecostal churches
groups.summary: Non-Trinitarian Pentecostal bodies (e.g. UPCI) splitting from Trinitarian Pentecostalism.

groups.name: Grace Communion International (ex–Worldwide Church of God)
groups.summary: Armstrong’s Radio/Worldwide Church of God; later trinitarian evangelical reformation as GCI; splinters remain.

groups.name: Independent Charismatic / neo-Pentecostal networks
groups.summary: Post-classical charismatic megachurches and apostolic networks; many have mixed Protestant parentage.
groups.notes: Lineage simplified; some emerge from Reformed/Baptist/Catholic charismatic streams.

groups.name: Jehovah’s Witnesses
groups.summary: Watch Tower society under Rutherford; distinct doctrines on Trinity, governance, eschatology.

groups.name: Vineyard Movement
groups.summary: Charismatic evangelical association founded by John Wimber et al.
